condition: subacute new onset frequent urination and excessive thirst in overweight adult
level_rationale: Three weeks of new-onset frequent urination and excessive thirst with fatigue today in an overweight 48-year-old adult points to subacute new-onset hyperglycemia requiring prompt outpatient general-physician evaluation and blood glucose testing rather than home self-care or emergency department care, whereas developing gasping breathing today on top of 3 weeks of polyuria and polydipsia signals acute metabolic acidosis or hyperglycemic crisis requiring immediate ER care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact hyperglycemic air-hunger escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Five strictly atomic reference facts cover age 48, overweight body habitus, 3 weeks of frequent urination, 3 weeks of excessive thirst, and feeling tired today, with an exact 14-vs-14 word span swap and 6 identical trailing tokens ('today so I should see a'). Replacing atomic fact f5 ('have felt tired') with 'started gasping for breath' stays inside the same new-onset hyperglycemic case and escalates care from outpatient physician evaluation (level 2) to acute metabolic crisis emergency care (level 4) with identical digit tokens and zero stated negatives.
